verdict_rationale: The technical observations in FV7-009 are confirmed from the pinned primary source: FatCountClustersInChain is an unbounded loop and BytesPerSector is assigned unvalidated. The engineering-packet promotion is not yet supported: no reproducer or runtime test has been executed, no maintainer feedback or canonical JIRA issue exists, and provenance/licensing per-file review is still pending. Accept the observation; require additional evidence before promoting.

line_evidence.verbatim: static ULONG FatCountClustersInChain(PFAT_VOLUME_INFO Volume, UINT32 StartCluster) { ULONG ClusterCount = 0; while (1) { if (FAT_IS_END_CLUSTER(StartCluster)) break; ClusterCount++; if (!FatGetFatEntry(Volume, StartCluster, &StartCluster)) return 0; } return ClusterCount; }
line_evidence.finding: Only exit paths are an end-of-chain marker (1119-1122) or a FAT read failure (1132-1135); there is no cluster-count or volume-size bound. A cyclic or self-referential cluster chain therefore loops without termination. Confirmed.
BytesPerSector is copied directly from the on-disk boot sector with no zero or power-of-two check; it is used as a divisor downstream. Confirmed.
FatNumberOfClusters is already defined at the pinned baseline, so the bound proposed in PR #9510 does not require a new helper.
